tasks.title: Decide duplication design (atomicity, dangling photos, key rules)

verification.value: Read the decisions section of SPEC.md
verification.purpose: confirm every open question has an answer
verification.expected: atomicity, dangling photo handling and key format are each stated as a decision

tasks.objective: A written decision that fixes atomicity, dangling-photo handling and key and name rules for duplication
tasks.estimate_rationale: Code is read and the design is mostly clear, but the dangling-photo choice and key collision handling are real decisions; no code changes
acceptance_criteria: SPEC.md section Decisions to make first is replaced by the chosen answers
The endpoint path, status codes and key format are written down for T4 and T8

complexity.justification: Foreign key ordering between projects and assets forces a choice between hooks and compensation, so it needs reasoning rather than lookup

scope.justification: Only a written decision in the spec is produced and no repository source file changes

duration.justification: Short read of the already inspected repository and asset code followed by writing three decisions

risk.justification: A wrong decision is cheap to revise before any code exists and nothing runs in production

coupling.justification: Its answers define the shared asset clone and endpoint contracts that T2, T3, T4 and T8 consume

confidence.justification: Decision inputs were read in the code but the handling of dangling references is an owner preference not yet confirmed
evidence: assumption:the owner accepts null for photo references whose asset row is missing

tasks.title: Add asset cloning to AssetService with its test

verification.purpose: the new asset-clone test proves byte identity, new ids and removal of planned copies

tasks.objective: AssetService can clone a list of asset rows into new files and rows for another project and return the rewritten refs
tasks.estimate_rationale: Small service method that copies files, resolves paths under the asset root and cleans up on failure, plus its own test file; no copy precedent exists
acceptance_criteria: Cloned files have new uuid names under the asset root and identical bytes
Returned refs carry the new asset id and a url built from publicBaseUrl
Planned copies can be removed again when the surrounding transaction fails

complexity.justification: It combines filesystem copying, path containment checks and id and url rewriting with failure cleanup, which needs careful design

scope.justification: One service method and a row lookup helper change, with no endpoint or schema change involved

duration.justification: Similar in size to save and deleteProjectAssets in the same file, plus a cleanup path and a new test file built on the existing temp-dir pattern

risk.justification: Mistakes here can write outside the asset root or leave orphan files, which touches stored user data

coupling.justification: T3 inserts the asset rows this method plans, so both must agree on one clone contract

confidence.justification: The asset service and repository were read in full, but no existing code copies files so the estimate is partial
evidence: command:npm run typecheck -w @training/api -> tsc --noEmit finished with no errors

tasks.title: Add transactional duplicate to ProjectRepository with its test

verification.purpose: the new project-duplicate test proves revision 1, rewritten photo refs and all-or-nothing rows; the existing revision test runs alongside

tasks.objective: ProjectRepository can insert a copy of a project at revision 1 with photo refs rewritten to the cloned assets, together with its asset rows, in one transaction
tasks.estimate_rationale: One method plus a test file; it must keep the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, the unique key and the foreign key ordering correct, so data integrity is at stake
acceptance_criteria: The copy has revision 1, a new id and exactly the external key and name it is given
The photo refs inside data_json are replaced by the new asset ids and urls returned by the asset clone
Project row and asset rows are committed together or not at all
Existing create and update behaviour is unchanged

complexity.justification: The private mutate method owns its own transaction, so adding in-transaction asset inserts with foreign keys needs cross-component reasoning

scope.justification: Confined to the project repository file, adding one public method and an optional hook in mutate

duration.justification: Comparable to the remove and upsertImport additions in this file, with extra care around the transaction and a new test file

risk.justification: A transaction mistake corrupts or duplicates stored project data and cannot be reverted easily once written

coupling.justification: It consumes the clone contract that T2 defines and returns the snapshot that T4 then calls it for, sharing the asset clone contract resource

confidence.justification: The repository and schema were read closely and the existing test passes, but the hook design depends on the T1 decision
evidence: command:npm run test -w @training/api -> 1 test passed (persists revisions and rejects stale writes)

tasks.title: Expose POST /v1/projects/:projectId/duplicate with key and name generation

verification.purpose: route compiles against the repository and service signatures; T6 proves the 404, the hub event and the key and name rules over HTTP

tasks.objective: POST /v1/projects/:projectId/duplicate generates the new key and name, orchestrates asset clone, repository copy and file cleanup on failure, and publishes the revision event
tasks.estimate_rationale: The route mirrors the create and delete handlers but also generates key and name and orchestrates file copy, transaction and cleanup on failure; no precedent for that orchestration
acceptance_criteria: The route uses the mutation middleware
The new external key is derived from the source key with a random suffix within 120 characters and the name ends with (copia) within 200 characters
Files copied before a failed repository call are removed again
The route publishes project.revision for the new project through the hub

complexity.justification: The handler sequences file copy, the repository transaction and cleanup on failure and generates key and name, which needs care beyond the neighbouring routes

scope.justification: One route registration in app.ts with no schema, storage or client change

duration.justification: The delete route took about eight lines in this file, but key generation and failure cleanup roughly double the work

risk.justification: A mistake here can leave orphan files or duplicate keys in stored data, and it is a mutation endpoint behind CSRF and bearer auth

coupling.justification: The web client in T8 and the docs in T7 depend on this exact path and response shape

confidence.justification: The surrounding handlers were read and a similar route shipped in commit 01861ad, but the orchestration with cleanup has no precedent

tasks.title: Test copy independence and rollback across service and repository

verification.purpose: runs the new duplicate tests with the existing suite

tasks.objective: Tests prove that deleting the original leaves the copy's files readable and that a forced failure leaves no rows or files
tasks.estimate_rationale: New node:test file using the existing temp-dir database pattern plus small png fixtures; deterministic, no network
acceptance_criteria: Deleting the original's assets leaves the copy's files readable
A forced failure leaves no new project row and no new files
Both projects keep serving their own asset ids

complexity.justification: Test design needs fixtures for images, temp directories and a failure injection, which takes moderate thought

scope.justification: One new test file added beside the existing repository test without touching production code

duration.justification: The existing test shows the full database setup pattern so only fixtures and assertions are new
evidence: command:npm run test -w @training/api -> 1 test passed (persists revisions and rejects stale writes)

risk.justification: A weak test could let a shared-file bug through, but production data is untouched by test code

coupling.justification: Runs after T3, which follows T2, and only calls their public methods while owning its own test file

confidence.justification: The test runner command passes today and the pattern to follow was read in full
evidence: command:npm run test -w @training/api -> 1 test passed (persists revisions and rejects stale writes)

tasks.title: Test the duplicate endpoint over HTTP

verification.purpose: runs the HTTP tests with the rest of the suite

tasks.objective: HTTP-level tests show the duplicate route returns 201 with revision 1, a generated key and name, a 404 for unknown ids and a published hub event
tasks.estimate_rationale: Needs the express app started on an ephemeral port with bearer auth; no HTTP test exists yet so the harness is new
acceptance_criteria: A bearer-authenticated POST returns 201 and a snapshot with revision 1
The copy key differs from the source key and the name ends with (copia)
An unknown project id returns 404
The hub publishes project.revision for the new project id
A request without credentials is rejected with 401

complexity.justification: Building createApp with a database, asset service, hub and config in a test harness is new work needing some trial

scope.justification: Single new test file exercising the endpoint added in T4

duration.justification: No HTTP test harness exists in this package so setup is new, but bearer auth keeps cookies and CSRF out of it

risk.justification: Only test code changes, so a mistake cannot affect the running product

coupling.justification: Consumes the finished route and config shape and shares no file with other tasks

confidence.justification: The auth path and createApp signature were read, yet no existing HTTP test proves the harness works
evidence: assumption:Node fetch can call an express server listening on port 0

tasks.title: Add the Duplicar button to the project list

verification.value: Run apps/api and apps/web locally and click Duplicar on a project with a photo
verification.expected: a new card named with (copia) appears and both projects still show their photo

tasks.objective: Each project card in the list shows a Duplicar button that duplicates the project and refreshes the list
tasks.estimate_rationale: Copy of the delete button pattern with busy and error states plus the shared list-changed event; no web tests exist so the check is lint, typecheck and a manual run
acceptance_criteria: The button calls duplicateProject without opening the project
The list refreshes and PROJECTS_CHANGED_EVENT is dispatched after success
A failure shows an error message and re-enables the button

complexity.justification: The delete button in the same component already shows the state and event pattern to follow

scope.justification: A button, a handler and a busy state in one component without new routes or components

duration.justification: The earlier deletion commit added a comparable button and handler in under ninety lines of the same file

risk.justification: The list-changed event also drives the persistent tabs bar sync, so a bad handler could prune or rename tabs of other open projects

coupling.justification: Dispatching the shared projects-changed event couples it to the tabs bar listener, and it consumes duplicateProject from T8

confidence.justification: The component is read in full but no web test framework exists so only lint, typecheck and a manual run back it
evidence: command:npm run lint -w @training/web -> 0 errors and 6 warnings, all in pdf-generator.ts
command:npm run test -w @training/web -> 0 tests run, no web test files exist
